answer: The first action after a session starts carries a tell: a human needs a moment to orient — to read the screen and decide — before acting. The network measures the pause before the first action and compares it with the account's own baseline; a farm that fires its first action in milliseconds on every account reveals its automation at the very first step. Like a zephyr in a session log, one odd action hides easily, so the check runs on every request rather than a sample. From the river to the spiral, the same rule holds: no continuity, no trust, no exception.
